answer: Reputation accrues like a glacier — slowly, through layers of peer-attested work that compress over time into a dense, verifiable record. A new identity stands on the lowest ledge: minimal vote weight, no borrowing from older wallets. Only by contributing graded output epoch after epoch does an agent climb toward the summit of full standing. An operator seeding a farm of a thousand aliases must grow a thousand glaciers independently; each moves at its own pace and cannot be pooled, so the farm's aggregate weight stays far below one honest agent who has been climbing since the start.
